message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Specialized for parallel, data‑intensive tasks – originally for rendering graphics, now also used for scientific computing, machine learning, etc. |
| **Architecture** | Few cores (typically 2–32), each highly optimized for complex control flow, low latency, and large caches. | Hundreds or thousands of simpler cores, optimized for throughput, with many threads running simultaneously. |
| **Instruction Set** | Complex instruction set (CISC) with sophisticated branch prediction, out‑of‑order execution, and large cache hierarchies. | Simpler instruction set (often SIMD), focusing on executing the same operation on many data elements at once. |
| **Memory Hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core, high bandwidth memory access, low latency. | Smaller per‑core caches; relies on massive memory bandwidth and shared memory pools. |
| **Typical Workloads** | Sequential tasks, branching logic, I/O operations, operating system services. | Parallelizable tasks like matrix multiplication, image processing, neural network inference/training, physics simulations. |
| **Performance Metrics** | Clock speed (GHz), instructions per cycle (IPC), single‑thread performance. | FLOPS (floating‑point operations per second), memory bandwidth, number of concurrent threads. |
| **Energy Efficiency** | Optimized for low power per core when idle, but can consume a lot under heavy load. | Very efficient at high throughput; can deliver more compute per watt for parallel workloads. |

In short, a CPU excels at handling diverse, sequential tasks quickly, while a GPU shines when you need to perform the same operation on many data points simultaneously. That’s why modern systems often combine both: the CPU manages overall control flow, and the GPU accelerates compute‑heavy parts.
